edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber I 4

source_text: Unguentum effusum nomen tuum. Nomen Iesu ubique diffusum est. Sicut unguentum fracto alabastro domum implet, sic Christi nomen orbe praedicato omnia replevit. Propterea adulescentulae dilexerunt te — animae incipientes et ecclesiae quae nuper crediderunt odore nominis eius attractae.
pass_a_gloss: Ointment poured-out name your. Name of-Jesus everywhere poured-out is. As ointment with-broken alabaster house fills, so of-Christ name with-world having-been-preached all-things filled. Therefore young-women loved you — souls beginning and churches which recently believed...
pass_b_english: [[Your name is ointment poured out >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:3]]. The name of Jesus has been poured out everywhere. As ointment, when the alabaster is broken, fills the house, so Christ’s name, when preached in the world, has filled all things. [[Therefore the young women have loved you >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:3]] — beginning souls and churches that have newly believed, drawn by the fragrance of his name.
